chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding lengthening the hair?' He said: 'The companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) were hairy (mush'irin), meaning the trimming (al-tamm).'

key_terms.الطَّمَّ: The trimming / cutting (referring to the act of trimming hair)
key_terms.مُشْعِرِينَ: Hairy / having full hair (a state of being)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the length of men's hair according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the term 'mush'irin' by linking it to the practice of the Prophet’s companions, who maintained a moderate hair length rather than letting it grow excessively long (a practice known as *tam*). This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ittida'* (trimming) as a sunnah of cleanliness and modesty, distinguishing it from the extreme of letting hair grow wild, which was often associated with specific pre-Islamic or later cultural styles.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding lengthening of the hair?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The companions of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> were hairy, meaning the trimming’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about growing long hairs. He (the Imam) said that companions of the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, clipped their hairs.’”
